response.rationale: Pathology (F10) definitively shows hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage, which is pathognomonic for torsion of the appendix testis. The presence of P. aeruginosa (F06) and enhanced vascularity (F07) likely represent secondary inflammation. Spermatic cord torsion (D3) is contradicted by the appendiceal location of infarction, and epididymo-orchitis (D2) is less likely given the pathology. The MRI finding (F09) supports chronic infarction rather than acute infection or neoplasm.
